title: 育儿与教育：成长型心态 — Day 2

questions.question: 孩子拿来一幅刚画好的画。按「表扬过程而非天赋」的建议，哪种说法最好？
options: 「画得真像，比班上其他小朋友画得都要好看！」
「不管画得怎么样，你都好努力，妈妈最喜欢了！」
「哇，你真是太有艺术天赋了，长大以后肯定能当个了不起的画家！」
「我注意到你在天空那里换了三种蓝色，是你自己试出来的吗？」
questions.explanation: 表扬过程要让孩子注意到自己做了什么具体决策，把成功归因于可控的策略。夸天赋会把自我价值和标签绑定；空洞的「你好努力」不真实、不具体，孩子反而觉得假；横向比较则把注意力引向结果和排名。
questions.question_en: A child brings over a picture they just finished. Following the advice to praise process rather than talent, which response is best?
options_en: 'It looks so real, way better than anyone else's in your class!'
'No matter how it turned out, you worked so hard, and I love it!'
'Wow, you're so artistically gifted, you'll definitely be a painter someday!'
'I noticed you used three different blues in the sky. Did you figure that out yourself?'
questions.explanation_en: Process praise helps the child notice the specific choices they made and attributes success to controllable strategies. Praising talent ties self-worth to a label; empty 'you worked so hard' is neither true nor specific and comes across as fake; comparing with classmates points attention at results and rank.

questions.question: 以下哪种做法属于对「成长型心态」的误用？
options: 把它当成「不许放弃」的工具，要求孩子无论什么事都必须坚持到底
孩子比赛输了先抱一抱共情，等情绪平稳后再一起复盘是哪段出了问题
放学不问考了几分，而是问「今天遇到的最难一道题，你怎么搞定的？」
在饭桌上讲一件自己工作中没做好的事，说说学到了什么、下次怎么试
questions.explanation: 真正的成长型心态包括判断一件事是否值得继续投入的智慧，把它变成「不许放弃」的强迫是误用。用过程性问题代替分数、先共情再复盘、父母示范自己如何从失败中学习，都是文中推荐的做法。
questions.question_en: Which of the following is a misuse of 'growth mindset'?
options_en: Using it as a 'never quit' rule and insisting the child must stick with everything to the end
After the child loses a match, hugging them first and reviewing what went wrong once they've calmed down
After school, instead of asking for the score, asking 'What was the hardest problem today, and how did you crack it?'
Telling the family at dinner about something you didn't do well at work, what you learned, and what you'll try next
questions.explanation_en: A genuine growth mindset includes the judgment to decide whether something is worth continuing; turning it into a compulsory 'never give up' is a misuse. Replacing scores with process questions, empathizing before reviewing, and parents modeling how they learn from their own failures are all practices the article recommends.
